The Honda Accord family

11 generations and variants in the Index, 1976–present. Oldest first; every card opens the full page, with its own versions, figures and story.

  1. 1976–1981

    Honda Accord (first generation)

    The first Accord, 1976–1981: a small, unusually well-equipped hatchback, then a sedan, that turned Honda from the maker of the Civic into a serious name in American driveways.

    68 hp13.8 sec 0-60731,927 built
    1.6-liter · 1.8-liter
  2. 1982–1985

    Honda Accord (second generation)

    The second-generation Accord, 1982–1985: the first car a Japanese company built in the United States, made at Honda's plant in Marysville, Ohio, from late 1982.

    86 hp12.5 sec 0-60942,731 built
  3. 1986–1989

    Honda Accord (third generation)

    The third-generation Accord, 1986–1989: pop-up headlights, double wishbones at all 4 corners, and a coupe built only in Ohio and shipped back to Japan.

    120 hp11.4 sec 0-601,385,250 built
  4. 1990–1993

    Honda Accord (fourth generation)

    The fourth-generation Accord, 1990–1993: bigger and smoother, with a fuel-injected 2.2-liter in every US car and, from 1991, a wagon built in Ohio.

    125 hp9.7 sec 0-601,539,983 built
  5. 1994–1997

    Honda Accord (fifth generation)

    The fifth-generation Accord, 1994–1997: dual airbags as standard, VTEC in the EX and, from 1995, the first V6 Accord.

    145 hp9.4 sec 0-601,475,906 built
    2.2-liter · 2.7-liter V6
  6. 1998–2002

    Honda Accord (sixth generation)

    The sixth-generation Accord, 1998–2002: split into separate cars for Japan, Europe and North America, with an American-designed coupe and a 200-hp VTEC V6.

    150 hp8.2 sec 0-602,023,476 built
    2.3-liter · 3.0-liter V6
  7. 2003–2007

    Honda Accord (seventh generation)

    The seventh-generation Accord, 2003–2007: i-VTEC 4-cylinders, a 240-hp V6 that coupe buyers could pair with a 6-speed manual, and the first Accord Hybrid.

    160 hp7.5 sec 0-601,900,485 built
    2.4-liter · 3.0-liter V6 · Hybrid
  8. 2008–2012

    Honda Accord (eighth generation)

    The eighth-generation Accord, 2008–2012: big enough that the EPA classed the sedan as a full-size car, with a 190-hp 4-cylinder and a 3.5-liter V6.

    190 hp8.2 sec 0-601,541,723 built
    2.4-liter · 3.5-liter V6
  9. 2013–2017

    Honda Accord (ninth generation)

    The ninth-generation Accord, sold for 2013–2017: the last Accord with a V6, the last with a coupe body, and the one that brought the Accord Hybrid back for 2017, rated at 48 mpg combined.

    185 hp7.6 sec 0-60127 mph top1,778,460 built
    2.4-liter · 3.5-liter V6 · Hybrid
  10. 2018–2022

    Honda Accord (tenth generation)

    The tenth-generation Accord, 2018–2022: lower, lighter and sharper, with a 192-hp 1.5-liter turbo, a 252-hp 2.0-liter turbo with a 10-speed automatic, a 212-hp hybrid and, through 2020, a 6-speed manual.

    192 hp7.3 sec 0-60121 mph top1,115,384 built
    1.5-liter turbo · 2.0-liter turbo · Hybrid
  11. 2023–present

    Honda Accord (eleventh generation)

    The eleventh-generation Accord, from 2023: a 192-hp turbo or, in most trims, a 204-hp hybrid rated at up to 48 mpg, with no V6, no 2.0T and no manual, and the first Honda with Google built-in.

    204 hp6.5 sec 0-60672,302 built
    Hybrid · 1.5-liter turbo
